narrative.intro: Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy has $232M in contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy has 3 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $77.3M. Obligations fell 22.6% year over year. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy received between $120M and $299M in annual obligations from FY21 through FY25, with specific fiscal-year totals of $120M in FY21, $274M in FY22, $196M in FY23, $244M in FY24, and $299M in FY25. Current-year totals are partial (fiscal year to date). Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy shows concentration in a few technical markets. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences is the largest market, followed by Optical Instrument and Lens Manufacturing, and a second Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences category for non-nanotechnology and non-biotechnology work.

sections.heading: How concentrated are obligations across markets?
sections.body: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences accounts for $134M in obligations. Optical Instrument and Lens Manufacturing accounts for $71.4M in obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) accounts for $26.2M in obligations.

sections.heading: How has annual funding changed since FY21?
sections.body: Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy obligations were $120M in FY21 and rose to $274M in FY22. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy obligations then moved to $196M in FY23, $244M in FY24, and $299M in FY25, before reaching $232M in FY26 to date. Obligations fell 22.6% year over year.
